summary: The Mountain Throne: a high kingdom of mines and forts at the end of the Sand Road, selling ore to the Pact or to any buyer.

mine_lords_council.name: The Council of Mine-Lords
mine_lords_council.desc: The lords of the deep seams sit at a table of black stone and vote with their ore-tallies. Queen Obmia listens, and then she decides.

crown_of_the_peaks_spirit.name: Crown of the Peaks
crown_of_the_peaks_spirit.desc: The Queen's crown is cut from the same grey stone as the mountain, and the peaks themselves seem to wear it. Her word runs in every shaft and on every ridge.

open_ore_market.name: The Open Ore Market
open_ore_market.desc: Any buyer with coin may bid for Erco's ore, and the auctions on the high square are watched from three kingdoms. The price rises every season, and so does the envy.

masters_of_iron_spirit.name: Masters of Iron
masters_of_iron_spirit.desc: Erco's smiths know a hundred ways of folding iron, and each house keeps its own ways in a locked chest. Their blades, plates and tools are known across the East.

mountain_realm.name: The Mountains Keep Their Own
mountain_realm.desc: The passes are narrow and the lords are many, and every trail has a fort on it. A host that comes to Erco finds the mountain already awake.

sand_road_markets.name: Markets of the Sand Road
sand_road_markets.desc: Where the Sand Road ends the markets begin, and every stall sells something that came a long way. Carters stay a night and spend a month's wages.

queens_consort.title: A Queen's Consort
queens_consort.desc: Queen Obmia has no consort, and the council of mine-lords has begun to speak of it. Plutondo's prince has sent a portrait, Ostoroth's king a letter, and the deep-seam lords a list of their own sons.

options.name: A mine-lord of our own mountains

focuses.name: The Mountain Throne
focuses.desc: Erco's queens have ruled from the high halls since before the caravan roads opened. Queen Obmia holds the throne by the loyalty of the mine-lords and the strength of her walls.

focuses.name: Queen Obmia's Council
focuses.desc: The council sits at the black table, the queen at its head and the mine-lords on either hand. Each lord brings an ore-tally, and each tally tells a different story.

focuses.name: The Mountain Clans
focuses.desc: The clans of the heights send their young men to the queen's banner every autumn. They bring goat-hair cloaks, iron-shod staves and a very long memory of old debts.

focuses.name: A Queen's Consort
focuses.desc: The question of a consort touches every lord and every road. Obmia hears the suits in her own time, and no suitor is told how it will end.

focuses.name: The High Halls
focuses.desc: The great hall is relit, its pillars rebuilt and its long tables relaid with silver. Envoys who climb the stair arrive out of breath and leave humbled.

focuses.name: Crown of the Peaks
focuses.desc: The old crown is reforged from the grey stone of the first seam, and the queen wears it at the midwinter court. The mine-lords kneel, one by one, and none of them has been forced.

focuses.name: The Mines of Erco
focuses.desc: Iron, silver and a little gold come out of Erco in rattling carts, and the pit-heads are never quiet. A new smelting-hall at the capital makes the best of it.

focuses.name: Deep Shafts
focuses.desc: Shafts go down past the old workings into stone no miner has seen. Lamp-men, rope-makers and prop-setters learn their trades from fathers who died young.

focuses.name: Foundries of Erco
focuses.desc: The foundry fires burn night and day beside the swift mountain streams, and ingots go down the slope in long lines. Smiths from three kingdoms come to buy.

focuses.name: Ore for the Pact
focuses.desc: Postondoroth's armouries and the Pact's forges take Erco's best ore at a price both sides can live with. The queen keeps Erco outside the Pact, but she keeps the Pact well supplied.

focuses.name: Ore for Any Buyer
focuses.desc: The ore goes to whoever pays most on the high square, and the queen's clerks write down the price and no names. Erco's neutrality is never so profitable as on auction day.

focuses.name: Smiths of the Heights
focuses.desc: The highest forges make plate and blade that the lowland smiths cannot match. Apprentices come from the sand cities to learn the hammer-turn, and stay for years.

focuses.name: Masters of Iron
focuses.desc: A guild of master smiths now stands above every forge, setting marks, grades and prices. Erco's iron is stamped, and a stamp from the high halls is trusted in every market.

focuses.name: Mountain Forts
focuses.desc: Every pass of Erco is closed by a fort, and every fort is within sight of the next. The queen's engineers add new towers where the old ones are weakest.

focuses.name: Hill Companies
focuses.desc: The hill companies muster at the passes and drill on the slopes, long spears in one hand and a sling in the other. Their captains grow grey on the rocks.

focuses.name: The High Passes Guarded
focuses.desc: Beacons are raised above the snow line, and guard-huts stand at every col. The watch is hard in winter, and the watchers are well paid for it.

focuses.name: Siege Engineers of Erco
focuses.desc: Erco's engineers can break a wall and mend one, and they teach both arts in the same school. Their trebuchets are carried in pieces on mule-back.

focuses.name: Walls of Erco
focuses.desc: The new walls are cut straight from the rock and set with iron pins. They are thick enough to stop a ram and plain enough to look like part of the mountain.

focuses.name: The Mountains Keep Their Own
focuses.desc: The old saying is read aloud in the high hall: what the mountains hold, the mountains keep. Erco's gates are shut to every host, whatever banner it carries.

focuses.name: The End of the Sand Road
focuses.desc: The Sand Road climbs out of the dunes and ends at a paved square under Erco's walls. Everything that has travelled this far has something to sell.

focuses.name: Caravans From Obmi
focuses.desc: Caravans from the southern desert bring dyes, glass and dried fruit, and take iron tools home. The carters sing as they enter the square.

focuses.name: The Mountain Road
focuses.desc: The last miles to the capital are paved, cambered and ditched on both sides. A loaded wagon no longer needs six oxen on the final grade.

focuses.name: Markets of the Heights
focuses.desc: Stall-keepers fill the square with cloth, ore and salt, and a covered hall is raised against the winter. The market-wardens keep the peace with brass staves.

focuses.name: The Last Well
focuses.desc: The last well on the Sand Road is sweet and deep, and carters bless it by name. Obmia has it walled, roofed and garrisoned, and its water is never sold.
